title: Full-Continuum Ultrafast Quantum Gas Microscopy
abstract: Quantum gas microscopy provides single-shot access to many-body configurations, but their microscopic reconstruction has so far largely relied on a predefined discrete spatial basis during fluorescence readout. Here we realize ultrafast atom-resolved fluorescence microscopy of an ultracold $^{162}$Dy gas directly in continuous space, with all external confinement removed during imaging. Exploiting the large mass and broad optical transition of dysprosium together with a high numerical aperture in-vacuum objective, we detect single atoms within $4\,\mu\mathrm{s}$ while maintaining an effective point-spread function with a full width at half maximum of $254.8(3)\,\mathrm{nm}$, and an isolated single-atom classification fidelity of $99.72(3)\%$. We use the measured single-atom response to construct a statistical configuration-inference model that recovers atomic positions and multiplicities, coming from overlapping atoms, directly from single fluorescence snapshots. Benchmarking our model on Monte-Carlo generated images shows a total reconstruction fidelity of $98.7\%$. Our approach extends quantum gas microscopy beyond predefined detection lattices, enabling atom-resolved measurements of counting statistics and higher-order spatial correlations directly on the intrinsic length scales of continuum many-body systems.

summaries.en: Researchers achieved ultrafast atom-resolved fluorescence microscopy of an ultracold dysprosium gas in continuous space with 4 microsecond detection, 254.

title: Electron-Mediated Phonon Polaritons in Quantum Cavities
abstract: Phonon-photon coupling in quantum materials is commonly treated as an effective direct interaction, neglecting the crucial role played by electrons. Here we develop a gauge-invariant theory of cavity phonon polaritons that captures electronic screening, dissipation, and hybridization. We show that screening can suppress polariton formation in metals, severely constraining cavity control of phonon-mediated superconductivity. By contrast, interband electronic resonances in time-reversal-symmetric gapped systems can strongly enhance phonon-photon coupling, enabling robust polariton formation down to the monolayer limit despite electronic absorption. We illustrate these effects in NbSe2, hBN, and gapped graphene. Finally, we show that gauge invariance enforces photon decoupling from a critical soft phonon, establishing a general no-go mechanism for photon condensation.

summaries.en: A gauge-invariant theory of cavity phonon polaritons shows that electronic screening suppresses polariton formation in metals while interband resonances in gapped systems enhance it, and that gauge invariance forbids photon condensation via critical soft phonons.

title: Nanoscale Mapping of Strain-engineered Excitons in Monolayer WSe$_2$
abstract: Excitons in monolayer transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) are highly sensitive to external stimuli, allowing control of resonance energies and lifetimes through electric and magnetic fields, heterostructures, moire potentials and mechanical strain. Observations of single-photon emission (SPE) near sample edges, wrinkles, and strained nanobubbles have motivated strain-engineering aimed at realizing localized emitters in 2D materials. The origin of these emitters remains unclear and prior studies have relied on far-field spectroscopy with strain profiles inferred separately through topography, limiting direct correlation between local strain and excitonic response. We directly probe strain-modified excitonic spectra in monolayer WSe$_2$ using cryogenic scattering-type scanning near-field optical microscopy (s-SNOM). We compare two strain-engineering techniques, nano-indentation and patterned substrates, used to produce SPEs. At 9 K, we spatially resolve exciton resonance shifts with sub-diffraction limit resolution, simultaneously measuring near-field optical response and topography. We observe that strain transferred from nano-indentation into a deformable polymer substrate differs from that produced by draping TMDs over patterned dielectric pillars. Adhesion and tearing during plastic deformation drive a compressive exciton blueshift, while draping produces dominant tensile strain. Comparing the strain model results to the experimentally observed energy shifts shows that the nano-indentation strain is over an order of magnitude smaller than previously inferred, due to puncturing of the fragile monolayer, whereas pillar-strained devices remain intact under more modest strain. These differences suggest SPE arises from complex, strain-mediated interactions rather than simple confinement potentials, establishing s-SNOM as a powerful probe of quantum emission in strained 2D materials.

summaries.en: Cryogenic scattering-type scanning near-field optical microscopy directly maps strain-modified exciton spectra in monolayer WSe2 at 9 K, revealing that nano-indentation produces over an order of magnitude less strain than previously inferred due to monolayer puncturing, whereas patterned-pillar draping yields intact, dominantly tensile strain.

title: Chern insulator optics
abstract: Chern insulators have optical properties that are strikingly different than ordinary chiral media. Unlike the natural optical activity of the latter, which is a finite-wavelength effect arising from spatial dispersion, the optical activity of a Chern insulator is already present in the long-wavelength limit, and exhibits a striking directional asymmetry in the propagation of circularly polarized light. We study this unnatural optical activity using a recently developed field theory for Chern insulators. For bulk Chern insulators, we derive the normal-incidence transmission and reflection coefficients of multilayer structures, identify the associated Faraday and Kerr angles, and show that these optical rotations provide a direct optical signature of topology at low frequencies. We also show that an interface between bulk Chern insulators can act as a kind of mirror, completely reflecting light at normal incidence when the Chern invariants have opposite signs. Moving to a more realistic model of a two-dimensional current sheet, we study the Faraday and Kerr effects in a thin film of $\mathrm{Mn}\mathrm{Bi}_2\mathrm{Te}_4$ in its Chern insulator phase. The predicted rotations are many orders of magnitude larger than those of optically active media of comparable thickness that are topologically trivial.

summaries.en: This paper uses a field theory to show that Chern insulators exhibit long-wavelength optical activity with directionally asymmetric circular polarization, enabling topological signatures via giant Faraday and Kerr rotations in thin films like MnBi2Te4.

title: Nonadiabatic dynamics under slow parametric modulation in nonlinear graphene resonators
abstract: Resonantly driven nonlinear systems, from superconducting circuits to nanomechanical resonators, are often described in a rotating frame, where amplitude and phase evolve slowly within a fixed landscape of stable and unstable states. How such systems behave when this landscape moves on their intrinsic timescale remains to be understood. Here, we exploit the strong tension sensitivity of a graphene drum's resonance frequency to reshape the rotating-frame phase space of a bistable mechanical mode in real time, combining an MHz-frequency resonant drive with kHz-frequency tension modulation. When the modulation rate becomes comparable to the mechanical relaxation rate, adiabatic tracking of the fixed points breaks down. Instead, parametric instabilities emerge in the slow dynamics at frequencies set by libration around these points rather than by the mechanical resonance; stronger modulation drives period doubling and chaos. A slow-variable theory predicts where the instabilities occur, and Melnikov analysis captures the onset of chaos. These results show that the rotating frame itself can be parametrically driven, offering a general route to controlling nonadiabatic dynamics in systems ranging from Josephson bifurcation amplifiers to cold atoms.
subjects: Mesoscale and Nanoscale Physics (cond-mat.mes-hall) ; Chaotic Dynamics (nlin.CD)

summaries.en: Slow parametric modulation of a graphene drum's tension drives the rotating-frame phase space of a bistable mechanical mode fast enough to break adiabatic tracking of fixed points, producing parametric instabilities, period doubling, and chaos governed by libration frequencies rather than the mechanical resonance.

title: Transverse magneto-gyrotropy driven by spin-induced ferroaxiality
abstract: Photon chirality is inherently sensitive to structural handedness and magnetism, which break spatial inversion and time-reversal symmetries, respectively. Ferroaxial order, by contrast, hosts two-dimensional chirality while preserving both symmetries, thereby precluding its direct coupling to photon chirality. Intertwining ferroaxiality with magnetic order, however, may lift such constraints and enable unconventional coupling to photon chirality. Nevertheless, the optical response arising from such intertwined order has yet to be demonstrated experimentally. Here, we demonstrate transverse magneto-gyrotropy arising from spin-driven ferroaxiality in the Weyl magnet EuCd2Sb2. Whereas the conventional polar magneto-optical Kerr effect is governed by magnetization parallel to the light-propagation direction, we observe a gyrotropic response associated with magnetization transverse to the light-propagation direction. The optical rotation exhibits a characteristic 120-degree periodicity upon rotation of the in-plane magnetic field, reflecting the threefold symmetry of the emergent ferroaxial state and revealing the ferroaxial origin of the transverse gyrotropic response. This coupling to photon chirality enables vectorial control of the gyrotropic response through the magnetic field direction. Our findings establish an interaction between photon chirality and transverse magnetization enabled by intertwined ferroaxial and magnetic orders, demonstrating a novel form of multiferroicity with functional light-matter interaction.

summaries.en: Transverse magneto-gyrotropy observed in the Weyl magnet EuCd2Sb2 reveals an unconventional coupling between photon chirality and transverse magnetization driven by spin-induced ferroaxiality, exhibiting a 120-degree periodicity that reflects the threefold symmetry of the emergent ferroaxial state.

title: Identification of carbon-related color centers in hBN by high-resolution ab initio photoluminescence modeling
abstract: Identification of optically active defects in hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) remains challenging because different defect candidates can produce similar calculated photoluminescence (PL) lineshapes. Here, we demonstrate that force-constant embedding methodology can be extended to calculate high-resolution, vibrationally resolved PL lineshapes in the polar layered material hBN. Benchmarking against the carbon dimer defect, responsible for the 4.1 eV emission, we show that the methodology accurately reproduces the low-energy acoustic phonons and fine spectral features that are inaccessible when using direct supercell calculations. Applying the methodology to neutral carbon trimers ($\mathrm{C_2 C_B}$ and $\mathrm{C_2 C_N}$), we find that the calculated PL lineshape and excitation energy of $\mathrm{C_2 C_N}$ closely match the low-temperature spectrum of the emitter with a zero-phonon line at 1.54 eV. These results establish high-resolution phonon-sideband modeling as a powerful tool for discriminating among candidate defects in polar materials.

title: Making Weak Interlayer Excitons Absorb: Manipulating the Effective Oscillator Strength via Purcell Engineering of Critical Coupling
abstract: Interlayer excitons (IXs) in transition metal dichalcogenide bilayers possess unique dipolar properties, providing a path for exploring correlated many-body phases, electrically tunable dipole-dipole interactions, and long-range exciton transport. However, the large electron-hole separation underlying their dipolar character also results in a significantly reduced oscillator strength, limiting their direct optical interaction with light, and thus the direct probing of their dynamics and many-body interactions. Here, we show that by using Purcell engineering of critical coupling, a weak interlayer transition can absorb as strongly as the dominant intralayer transition, despite its much smaller intrinsic oscillator strength. Using this approach, in an open cavity architecture we demonstrate an order of magnitude IX absorption modulation in bilayer and trilayer MoS2, with doubling of the IX to A-exciton interaction strength weight from ~23% to ~53%. Furthermore, we demonstrate that in a tailored closed cavity architecture, the IX enhancement can reach beyond an order of magnitude, from ~5% to ~83% excitonic absorption, enabling IX absorption similar to intralayer excitons. An analytical description of the interaction is obtained via a closed-form transmission-line model which separates the excitonic and photonic contributions to the optical response, revealing how cavity architecture can be designed towards critical coupling. Our findings establish Purcell engineering of critical coupling as a general route to controlling and enhancing weak excitonic transitions.
subjects: Mesoscale and Nanoscale Physics (cond-mat.mes-hall) ; Other Condensed Matter (cond-mat.other); Optics (physics.optics)

summaries.en: Purcell engineering of critical coupling enables weak interlayer excitons in MoS2 bilayers to absorb as strongly as dominant intralayer excitons, achieving up to ~83% excitonic absorption in a tailored closed cavity.

title: Dynamic morphing of non-Euclidean active shells enabled by flutter under a steady stimulus
abstract: Synthetic active surfaces are usually designed to attain a prescribed static configuration, with dynamic shape changes typically requiring modulation of the actuation. We show that thin active shells can instead sustain dynamic morphing under a steady stimulus by harnessing flutter instability. We focus on polyelectrolyte hydrogel shells immersed in a viscous fluid and subjected to a constant and uniform electric field, and specialize the non-Euclidean framework for thin structures to account for field-induced activity through a spontaneous curvature evolving in time with the system configuration. Examining elliptic plates and cylindrical shells as test cases, we integrate linear stability analyses with nonlinear simulations to first locate the onset of flutter and then unveil the resulting dynamics, characterized by thrust-generating shape changes. In all cases, the emergent behavior stems from the interplay between active reconfiguration and elasticity in the fluid environment. For plates, the problem is purely flexural in the linear regime, while the competition between bending and stretching becomes crucial in selecting the ensuing shapes and swimming trajectories at large deformations. Conversely, for cylindrical shells bending and stretching are coupled at all levels, with the latter becoming essential to sustain flutter. Experiments on millimeter-sized hydrogel plates provide tangible support for our theoretical findings through shape reconstructions performed by combining digital image correlation with optical stereo microscopy. Flutter thus offers a route to untethered soft robotic and microfluidic devices based on active shells and operating under a stimulus carrying neither an intrinsic frequency nor a characteristic length scale.

summaries.en: Thin active shells made of polyelectrolyte hydrogel can undergo sustained dynamic morphing and thrust-generating shape changes under a constant uniform electric field by harnessing a flutter instability, as shown by combining linear stability analysis, nonlinear simulations, and optical stereo-microscopy experiments on millimeter-sized plates.

title: Anyons at impurities: Fractional charge measurement and "wrong sign" binding
abstract: Recent photoluminescence experiments in twisted MoTe$_2$ have reported signatures of anyons binding to trapped trions. The measured binding energies near the fractional Chern insulators at fillings of $\nu=-2/3$ and $-3/5$ have a ratio close to the fractional-charge ratio $5/3$, even though such scaling is not generally guaranteed for the expected short-range trion-anyon interaction. We model the trapped trion as a fixed impurity, and investigate anyon-impurity binding using a lowest-Landau-level model with exact diagonalization and Jain wavefunctions. Surprisingly, we find that the anyon-impurity binding energy ratio between $\nu=-2/3$ and $-3/5$ is close to $5/3$ for either short- or long-ranged impurity-electron interactions. However, the ratio departs strongly from the charge ratio at intermediate ranges or different Jain states. Remarkably, we also uncover "wrong-sign" binding, whereby both quasiholes and quasiparticles can bind to either sign of a short-range impurity potential by selecting orbital channels with favorable local density oscillations. Our findings show that localized excitons or trions can be used to probe the internal density profile of anyons.
subjects: Strongly Correlated Electrons (cond-mat.str-el) ; Mesoscale and Nanoscale Physics (cond-mat.mes-hall)

summaries.en: Exact diagonalization and Jain wavefunction calculations of anyon-impurity binding in a lowest-Landau-level model show that the binding energy ratio between ν=-2/3 and -3/5 approaches the fractional-charge ratio 5/3 for short- or long-ranged interactions but deviates at intermediate ranges, and reveal "wrong-sign" binding where quasiholes and quasiparticles both bind to either sign of a short-range impurity potential.

title: Supercell-enabled inverse design of boundary-state dispersion for group-velocity control in pseudomagnetic phononic crystals
abstract: Topological boundary states offer a platform for guided-wave propagation within bulk bandgaps. Their propagation characteristics depend not only on the spectral extent of the states but also on their dispersion within the operating bandwidth. A nearly linear dispersion provides more uniform group velocity across frequency, whereas a reduced slope enables slow-wave propagation. Despite advances in inverse design of prescribed dispersion relations and topological dispersion tuning, application-oriented characteristics of boundary-state dispersion have rarely been direct inverse-design objectives. Here, we develop a supercell-enabled, surrogate-assisted framework for the inverse design of boundary-state dispersion in a phononic crystal with pseudomagnetic fields. Area-preserving anisotropic deformation shifts the local Dirac points, and independent variation of 21 rows within the supercell provides distributed control over the boundary-state branch. A constraint-preserving surrogate reconstructs the dispersion from an initial frequency and positive frequency increments, with first- and second-difference losses introduced to capture local slope and curvature. Coupled with a genetic algorithm, the framework targets two prescribed-bandwidth design tasks: highly linear dispersion and slow-wave dispersion. For the former, finite-element verification yields relative group-velocity variations of 0.142% to 1.183% over prescribed bandwidths of 4% to 6%. For slow-wave designs, mean group velocities of 190 to 385 m/s are obtained over bandwidths of 0.2% to 0.8% while satisfying a 5% group-velocity variation limit. These results establish boundary-state dispersion as a direct inverse-design target beyond conventional bandwidth optimization, opening a flexible route to group-velocity control through application-oriented dispersion engineering over prescribed relative bandwidths.

title: High-resolution retinal matrix imaging via computational motion and aberration correction
abstract: High-resolution optical imaging of the human retina is essential for diagnosing ophthalmic and neurodegenerative diseases. While adaptive optics combined with coherence gating can resolve retinal structures at the cellular scale, it requires complex, costly, and cumbersome hardware to physically correct for ocular aberrations and motion. Matrix imaging offers a powerful digital alternative by leveraging wave linearity to undo aberrations and multiple scattering; however, its in vivo deployment has been hindered by continuous, involuntary eye movements that destroy phase coherence during acquisition. Here, we overcome this fundamental barrier and demonstrate the first in vivo reflection matrix imaging of the human retina using an ultra-simplified optical setup without physical correctors. We introduce a fully computational framework that tracks and compensates for multi-axial ocular motion directly from raw interferometric data, thereby restoring the phase coherence of a multi-spectral distortion matrix. This enables local, high-order aberration correction to achieve diffraction-limited, volumetric imaging of retinal tissues. By shifting the hardware burden to physics-guided numerical computation, this paradigm opens the way for accessible, non-invasive, and high-resolution digital ophthalmology.
subjects: Optics (physics.optics) ; Image and Video Processing (eess.IV); Applied Physics (physics.app-ph); Medical Physics (physics.med-ph)

summaries.en: This work demonstrates the first in vivo reflection matrix imaging of the human retina with an ultra-simplified setup, using a fully computational framework to track and compensate multi-axial ocular motion and thereby restore phase coherence for diffraction-limited volumetric imaging.

title: Topologically Protected Surface Acoustic Wave Edge States in Phononic Integrated Circuits
abstract: Phononic integrated circuits enable the development of compact systems to manipulate radio frequency signals through interconnected networks of acoustic waveguides. Introducing topologically protected robustness in these circuits to counter fabrication imperfections and local perturbations, remains a challenge. This work presents a validated modeling framework for topologically protected edge states using surface acoustic waves in etch-defined waveguides consisting of scandium aluminum nitride on silicon carbide, directly comparing analytical, full-wave numerical simulation, and laser Doppler vibrometer measured experimental approaches and their agreement. This work represents the first experimental demonstration of topological edge states on a ScAlN on SiC platform, validated through direct quantitative comparison with analytical and numerical analyses, with future implications for topological protection in phononic and optomechanical integrated circuit platforms.

summaries.en: This work experimentally demonstrates topologically protected surface acoustic wave edge states in etch-defined scandium aluminum nitride on silicon carbide waveguides, with analytical and full-wave numerical models quantitatively validated by laser Doppler vibrometer measurements.
summaries.zh: 本研究在碳化硅上的钪铝氮蚀刻波导中实验演示了拓扑保护的表面声波边缘态，并通过激光多普勒振动计测量对解析和全波数值模型进行了定量验证。

title: Combined Absorption and Emission Study of Air Species in NASA EAST
abstract: A suite of tunable diode laser absorption spectroscopy (TDLAS) diagnostics targeting rovibrational states of nitric oxide (NO) in the mid-infrared (MIR) and electronic states of atomic oxygen (O) and nitrogen (N) in the near-IR (NIR) was combined with optical emission spectroscopy (OES) for overlapping wavelengths at the NASA Electric Arc Shock Tube (EAST) facility for three selected high-temperature air experiments. Absorption features were probed at rates up to 1 MHz to provide quantitative, time-resolved measurements of temperature and species number density profiles behind incident shocks, enabling comparisons to spatially-resolved emission measurements, with the two typically agreeing within their respective uncertainties. Inferred time-histories are further compared to incident shock simulations from two one-dimensional models - one leveraging the Park two-temperature rates and the other more recent rate values - as well as the Data Parallel Line Relaxation (DPLR) code. For the two low-velocity cases (3.81 and 3.98 km/s) in which NO is probed, inferred temperatures are typically well-captured by all three models, although the NO number densities show stronger variation, agreeing better for the model with updated NO formation and dissociation rates. Finally, one high-velocity case (7.03 km/s) demonstrates the simultaneous resolution of three O-atom and six N-atom electronic states, with all states showing a steady increase in number density over time - possibly due to shock trajectory effects. Together, this combined absorption and emission study demonstrates resolution of many states of nonequilibrium air species, while directly comparing ground- and excited-state populations via the combined diagnostic strategy.

summaries.en: A combined TDLAS and OES study at NASA EAST resolved time-resolved temperature and number densities of NO, O, and N behind incident shocks in high-temperature air, showing good agreement between absorption and emission measurements and with 1D simulations.
summaries.zh: 在NASA EAST设施上结合TDLAS与OES的联合诊断研究，实现了高温空气激波后NO、O和N的时间分辨温度与数密度测量，吸收与发射结果及一维模拟均表现出良好一致性。

title: Strong field confinement in air and enhanced optical Kerr nonlinearity of high-index star-shaped pore membrane metasurfaces
abstract: The optical Kerr effect in high-refractive-index membrane metasurfaces patterned with a square lattice of five-pointed star-shaped pores is investigated numerically using gallium phosphide as a model material. The star geometry supports resonances with pronounced electromagnetic energy confinement, including an anapole state. The sharp tips of the star-shaped pores concentrate the electric energy density in air, exceeding that of Mie voids by a factor of seven. The effective second-order refractive index is enhanced by up to three orders of magnitude relative to bulk GaP, with the largest values obtained near the anapole resonances. The nonlinear response remains stable under polarization rotation and random misalignment of the nanoholes, indicating tolerance to fabrication imperfections. These results establish star-shaped pore lattices in freestanding membranes as a promising platform for nonlinear optics exploiting strong field confinement.

summaries.en: High-index star-shaped pore membrane metasurfaces exhibit strong electric field confinement in air and enhanced optical Kerr nonlinearity, with the effective second-order refractive index increased by up to three orders of magnitude relative to bulk GaP near anapole resonances, while remaining stable under polarization rotation and random misalignment.

title: A compact six-beam 3D magneto-optical trap based on multifunctional metasurface chips
abstract: Magneto-optical traps (MOTs), indispensable to cold-atom-based quantum computing and quantum precision measurement, are increasingly desired in compact and stable form. Particularly, the six-beam 3D-MOT, distinguished by symmetric geometry and superior trapping performance, finds particularly broad applications. Conventional implementations, however, rely on complex and bulky free-space optics, hindering miniaturization, practical assembly, and long-term stability. Here, we demonstrate a compact six-beam 3D-MOT system that employs two multifunctional optical metasurface chips to implement the optical-field functionalities required for cooling and trapping atoms. By combining two metasurface chips and a vacuum cell, a photonic-integrated cell module (PICM) is implemented as the core assembly and the volume is only" 73*73*107 mm^3" . In success, 1.3 * 10^3 Rb atoms are trapped and cooled to the temperature of ~183 {\mu}K. It should be noticed that the laser beam is guided to the metasurface through optical fiber, thus such fully fiber-coupled architecture enables straightforward and stable operations. We believe that this work would pave a practical route toward compact and portable 3D-MOT.

title: Femtosecond all-optical polarization manipulation of harmonic generation in an anisotropic strongly coupled plasmon-epsilon-near-zero metasurface
abstract: Ultrafast manipulation of light polarization plays a key role in modern high-speed photonics and optoelectronic operations. However, most current polarization-active modulation schemes are restricted by a limited operating wavelength range (visible to infrared), narrow-band resonant fundamental wavelength working condition, and relatively long modulation time (> 1 picosecond). Here, by taking advantage of the transient anisotropic nonlinearity of optical strong coupling between the epsilon-near-zero mode of indium tin oxide (ITO) film and polarization-selective plasmonic resonance, we achieve femtosecond polarization manipulation of broadband light that spans ultraviolet (UV) to visible region by controlling harmonic generation of the signal light under resonant pumping. We demonstrate polarization elliptic rotation of 23.3° at 407 nm for third-harmonic generation (THG) and 55.0° at 610 nm for second-harmonic generation (SHG) simultaneously within ~600 fs. In addition, the strongly coupled system can also serve as a universal femtosecond polarization modulation source, imprinting a 32.9° polarization rotation in the UV region by converting the modulation information of the fundamental signal light to that of THG light via a uniform ITO film in a cascaded configuration. Our study establishes a new paradigm for UV-based, ultrahigh-speed broadband polarization photonics with direct implications for high-speed optical information processing and programmable nonlinear photonic devices.

summaries.en: By exploiting the transient anisotropic nonlinearity of strong coupling between an epsilon-near-zero ITO film mode and a polarization-selective plasmonic resonance, femtosecond all-optical polarization manipulation is achieved, producing 23.

title: Two-Photon Spatial Multiplexing: Image Encoding in Gaussian Noncircularity of Light
abstract: The search for new degrees of freedom (DoF) of light is central to advancing optical information encoding and multiplexing. Gaussian statistics are ubiquitous in nature, and here we unlock an unexpected statistical DoF in the joint noncircularity of Gaussian light. For a pair of Gaussian light fields, the covariance- and pseudocovariance-dominated two types of correlations dictate the propagation rules and the image-encoding responses, mapping optical information into coordinate-difference and coordinate-sum momentum spaces, respectively. A hybrid random-phase grating array enables the experimental preparation of noncircular Gaussian light with programmable coexistence, yielding X-shaped intensity correlations while subtly reducing the degree of second-order coherence. Two independently programmed images coexist in the same beams at identical wavelength and polarization, yet are selectively decoded through two-photon correlation geometry without physical filters. Remarkably, both images remain recoverable even when structured stray light is as intense as the signal. These results unlock a hidden statistical dimension of optical information encoding, transforming Gaussian fluctuations into a dual-channel information carrier and joint noncircularity into a programmable optical DoF.

summaries.en: By exploiting the joint noncircularity of Gaussian light, two-photon spatial multiplexing encodes two independently programmable images in the covariance and pseudocovariance correlations of the same beam, allowing selective decoding without physical filters even under strong stray light.
summaries.zh: 通过利用高斯光的联合非圆性，双光子空间复用将两幅独立可编程图像编码在同一光束的协方差与伪协方差关联中，从而无需物理滤波器即可选择性解码，即使在强杂散光下也能恢复图像。
summaries.ja: ガウス光の合同非円形性を利用した二光子空間多重化により、同一ビームの共分散相関と擬共分散相関に二つの独立にプログラム可能な画像を符号化し、強い迷光下でも物理フィルターなしで選択的に復号できる。

title: Computational compressive imaging reconstruction with a simulated-annealing-based Ising solver
abstract: Computational compressive imaging, such as single-pixel imaging and lensless imaging, is a promising imaging technique, enabling the reconstruction of objects from under-sampled measurements through compressed sensing algorithms or deep learning methods. However, the demand for electronic computational resources grows rapidly when recovering high-resolution and multi-dimensional images and training neural networks with numerous parameters, which has become a bottleneck for the widespread adoption of this technique. Here, we propose a physics-driven reconstruction framework that formulates imaging inverse problems as Ising models and directly recovers target objects through the self-evolution of non-von Neumann Ising machines toward the ground state of the Hamiltonian. We employ a simulated-annealing-based Ising solver to demonstrate this proof-of-concept by reconstructing objects in both single-pixel imaging and a lensless diffuser camera at sampling rates ranging from 1% to 25%. By further incorporating a foreground-sparsity constraint and a smoothness constraint, the reconstruction quality of our method is comparable to or even better than that of mainstream algorithms. This approach has the potential to substantially reduce the electronic computational burden of inverse reconstruction, paving the way for real-time, low-power computational imaging.
subjects: Optics (physics.optics) ; Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV); Distributed, Parallel, and Cluster Computing (cs.DC); Mathematical Physics (math-ph); Applied Physics (physics.app-ph)

summaries.en: This paper proposes a physics-driven reconstruction framework that formulates computational compressive imaging inverse problems as Ising models and solves them with a simulated-annealing-based Ising solver, achieving reconstruction quality comparable to or better than mainstream algorithms in single-pixel and lensless diffuser imaging at sampling rates of 1% to 25% while potentially reducing the electronic computational burden.
summaries.zh: 本文提出了一种物理驱动的重建框架，将计算压缩成像的逆问题建模为伊辛模型，并利用基于模拟退火的伊辛求解器直接求解，在1%至25%的采样率下于单像素成像和无透镜漫射相机中实现了与主流算法相当甚至更优的重建质量，有望降低逆重建的电子计算负担。

title: Preservation of photon statistics upon selective molecular modulation in hollow-core fibers
abstract: Preserving the underlying statistical properties of light during frequency transduction is essential for interfacing spectrally disparate quantum systems. To do this successfully, the process needs to be highly efficient, broadband and noiseless. Despite significant progress in this field, satisfying all these conditions remains challenging. Recently, molecular modulation-based transduction in hollow-core fibers has emerged as a promising approach, where biphoton correlations were proven to be preserved during frequency up-conversion. However, beyond this previous demonstration of correlation-maintaining conversion, whether molecular modulation can preserve more general statistical properties of light remains experimentally unexplored. Here, we demonstrate the conservation of photon-number statistics during selective frequency transduction by Raman molecular modulation in a hydrogen-filled hollow-core fiber. As a proof of concept, weak 585-nm signals are selectively converted to 773 nm in the near-infrared and to 471 nm in the blue spectral region with near-unity efficiencies. Phase matching between the generated coherence waves and the transitions of interest is achieved through the effective dispersion of the system, enabling independent selection of the frequency up- and down-conversion processes. The preservation of the photon-number statistics of the shifted signals, along with the large frequency shifts, broad tunability and compatibility with quantum-optical fields, provides a versatile fiber-based platform for quantum frequency transduction. In particular, the demonstrated interfacing between visible and near-infrared wavelengths using low pump energies and low gas pressures offers a route towards connecting spectrally distinct quantum systems, including quantum emitters, sensors and atomic quantum memories, within hybrid quantum networks.

summaries.en: Researchers demonstrated that Raman molecular modulation in a hydrogen-filled hollow-core fiber can selectively convert weak 585-nm signals to 773 nm and 471 nm with near-unity efficiency while preserving the photon-number statistics, offering a versatile platform for quantum frequency transduction between visible and near-infrared wavelengths.
summaries.zh: 研究人员证明，在充氢空芯光纤中通过拉曼分子调制，可将弱的585纳米信号以接近 unity 的效率选择性转换至773纳米和471纳米，同时保持光子数统计特性，为可见光与近红外波长之间的量子频率转换提供了通用平台。
summaries.ja: 研究者らは、水素充填中空コアファイバーにおけるラマン分子変調により、弱い585nm信号を773nmおよび471nmへほぼ unity の効率で選択的に変換しつつ光子数統計を保持することに成功し、可視光と近赤外の間の量子周波数変換のための汎用プラットフォームを提供した。

title: High-Harmonic Generation Probes Quantum Nuclear Fluctuations in Liquid Water
abstract: Nuclear quantum effects are essential for an accurate description of the hydrogen-bonded structure of liquid water, yet their spectroscopic signatures can be subtle and difficult to measure. Moreover, probing these effects in solution on femtosecond timescales (or below) is an open challenge that is pivotal for optical control of hydrogen bonds and ultrafast spectroscopy of proton transfer. Here, we combine path-integral molecular dynamics with real-time time-dependent density-functional theory to explore high-harmonic generation (HHG) in liquid water from first principles, rigorously accounting for quantum nuclear delocalisation. Relative to classical-nuclei simulations, quantum sampling suppresses the harmonic yield around certain harmonics by up to an order of magnitude, inducing local structural minima. By analysing the ab initio simulations and reproducing the key effects with a simplified model Hamiltonian, we trace the physical origins of the interference minima to the broadening of valence-band states induced by hydrogen-bond fluctuations, a mechanism expected to generalise to other hydrogen-bonded structures. Our work shows that nuclear quantum effects are indispensable for capturing ultrafast electronic dynamics in liquids, and demonstrates the power of liquid HHG spectroscopy for attosecond probing of nuclear fluctuations.

summaries.en: First-principles simulations combining path-integral molecular dynamics with real-time time-dependent density-functional theory reveal that quantum nuclear delocalization in liquid water suppresses high-harmonic generation yields by up to an order of magnitude and creates interference minima arising from hydrogen-bond-induced broadening of valence-band states.
summaries.zh: 结合路径积分分子动力学与实时含时密度泛函理论的第一性原理模拟表明，液态水中的量子核离域使高次谐波产率在特定谐波附近降低达一个数量级，并产生由氢键涨落引起的价带态展宽所导致的干涉极小值。
summaries.ja: 経路積分分子動力学と実時間時間依存密度汎関数理論を組み合わせた第一原理計算により、液体水中の量子核非局在化が特定の高調波付近で高次高調波発生の収率を最大一桁低下させ、水素結合揺らぎに起因する価電子帯状態の広がりに由来する干渉極小を生じることが明らかになった。

title: Inferring Transition-Dipoles from Two-Dimensional Infrared Spectroscopy with Deep Learning
abstract: Two-dimensional infrared (2D IR) spectroscopy is a powerful nonlinear technique for probing vibrational couplings, anharmonicities, coherence, and molecular dynamics. Among the microscopic parameters encoded in 2D IR spectra, transition dipoles are fundamental quantities that characterize molecular structure and govern light-matter interactions. However, reconstructing these quantities from spectroscopic data remains a challenging inverse problem. Here, we introduce a physics-informed convolutional neural network (CNN), Spec2DipoleNet, trained on 2D IR spectra generated via the non-Hermitian Hamiltonian (NHH) method. This multi-task CNN reconstructs the transition dipole matrices under physically-motivated masking constraints. On the validation set, the model achieves a root-mean-square error (RMSE) of 0.085, an $R^2$ of 0.97, and a normalized cross-correlation of 0.98. It reliably recovers matrix elements associated with allowed transitions, while larger deviations are observed for nominally forbidden transitions. Our results suggest that transition dipole operators can be quantitatively inferred from 2D IR spectra, highlighting the potential of physics-informed deep learning for extracting microscopic quantum parameters from multidimensional spectroscopic data.

title: Interactive event-driven 4D-STEM with Timepix4 and live analytical ptychography
abstract: Four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy provides access to rich diffraction information at every probe position, but the high data rates associated with pixelated detectors remain a major challenge for interactive operation. Event-driven detectors offer an efficient alternative by representing the measurement as a sparse stream of individual incidences, substantially reducing requirements related to data handling and enabling on-the-fly processing. Here, we develop a high-throughput, real-time, 4D-STEM workflow based on the Timepix4 detector and demonstrate its operation at microsecond dwell times and standard beam currents. A common clock shared by the scan unit and detector allows the probe position of each electron event to be determined directly from its time-of-arrival, eliminating the need for inter-stream synchronization and enabling fully concurrent and independent multi-stream processing. The resulting pipeline continuously processes the detector data during acquisition, with the reconstructed images directly available. We demonstrate live virtual annular detector imaging, Real-Time Integration Center of Mass and direct electron ptychography within the guided progressive reconstructive imaging framework. The workflow sustains the high event rates of Timepix4 while maintaining zero latency for live interactive operation, thus extending event-driven 4D-STEM towards beam currents and acquisition conditions beyond those previously demonstrated with Timepix3-based systems. These results demonstrate that the combination of high-bandwidth event-driven detection, hardware-level synchronization and parallel processing can transform 4D-STEM from an offline technique into an interactive imaging modality, in which dose-efficient phase contrast and diffraction-based signals can serve directly as immediate feedback during STEM experiments.

summaries.en: The paper develops a real-time, event-driven 4D-STEM workflow using the Timepix4 detector with a shared clock and parallel multi-stream processing to achieve zero-latency live analytical ptychography at microsecond dwell times and standard beam currents.
summaries.zh: 本文开发了一种基于Timepix4探测器的实时事件驱动4D-STEM工作流程，通过共享时钟和并行多流处理，在微秒级驻留时间和标准束流下实现零延迟的实时分析型叠层成像。
summaries.ja: 本論文は、Timepix4検出器を用いたリアルタイムのイベント駆動型4D-STEMワークフローを開発し、共有クロックと並列マルチストリーム処理により、マイクロ秒のドウェル時間と標準的なビーム電流でゼロレイテンシのライブ解析的タイコグラフィを実現した。

title: Bias-Modulated Electronically-Tunable Optoelectronic Chromatic Dispersion in Ge PN Photodiodes
abstract: Optoelectronic Chromatic Dispersion (OED) is a source of significant wavelength-dependent current in photodiodes, offering a pathway to computational spectroscopy in a photodiode-only platform without the need for additional optical or mechanical components. Previous studies have activated OED through light modulation. Here, we present a theoretical and experimental investigation of bias-modulated OED in the C- and L-bands in a Ge PN photodiode, where the applied bias voltage is modulated sinusoidally, and the optical illumination is held constant. The spectral response is due to wavelength-dependent optical absorption together with bias-dependent competition between carrier drift, displacement current, and mobile-charge screening. With the RF phase-shift technique, the maximum measured OED sensitivity is +4.13 deg/nm in the L-band, significantly larger than that of light-modulated OED in Ge. The 15 mdeg phase-noise floor yields a spectral resolution of 3.6 pm. These results establish bm-OED as an electronically reconfigurable dispersive mechanism for applications in chip-scale computational spectrometers, photonic integrated circuits (PICs), on-chip RF photonics, and wavelength-division multiplexing.

summaries.en: This paper theoretically and experimentally demonstrates bias-modulated optoelectronic chromatic dispersion in a Ge PN photodiode, achieving a maximum sensitivity of +4.

summaries.ja: 本論文では、Ge PNフォトダイオードにおけるバイアス変調光電子波長分散を理論的および実験的に実証し、波長依存吸収とバイアス依存のキャリアダイナミクスにより、Lバンドで最大+4.

title: Polaritonic self-hybridized critical coupling by Brillouin zone folding induced quasi-bound states in the continuum in bulk WS2 metasurfaces
abstract: Maximizing the absorption of exciton-polaritons in transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs) under critical coupling conditions is crucial for developing high-efficiency polariton-based photodetectors, solar cells, and perfect absorbers. Here, we propose a polaritonic critical self-hybridized coupling between Brillouin zone folding driven quasi-bound states in the continuum (BZF-QBIC) mode and A excitons in a bulk WS2 metasurface. This polaritonic critical coupling shows robust behavior with respect to the asymmetric parameters of the involved BZF-QBIC mode, in contrast to the asymmetry-sensitive conventional QBIC-based critical coupling. By changing the height of WS2 metasurfaces, we observe a typical anti-crossing behavior with a Rabi splitting of 246.5 meV. Moreover, the maximum absorption value of 0.5 for exciton-polaritons is achieved at the polaritonic critical coupling condition. The large population of excitons provided by bulk WS2 is essential for achieving polaritonic critical coupling and can further enhance polaritonic absorption. This work enables the realization of robust, high-absorption self-hybridized polaritonic critical coupling in TMDCs, and further expedite their applications in high-absorption low-dimensional polaritonic devices.

summaries.en: This work demonstrates polaritonic critical self-hybridized coupling between Brillouin zone folding induced quasi-bound states in the continuum and A excitons in bulk WS2 metasurfaces, achieving a Rabi splitting of 246.

title: Near-field contributions to cavity-mediated radiative heat transfer
abstract: Embedding materials in optical cavities has emerged as a powerful strategy for controlling their physical properties. In this context, increasing attention has been devoted to the thermal Purcell effect, which describes how the radiative heat transfer between a material and its photonic environ- ment can be modified by the electromagnetic boundary conditions imposed by the cavity. Here, we investigate near-field effects in cavity-mediated radiative heat transfer in planar cavities composed of realistic, dissipative gold mirrors, extending previous work that considered ideal mirrors. We iden- tify the conditions under which near-field effects lead to a substantial enhancement of heat transfer between the material and a photonic thermal bath relative to free space, owing to the strong modi- fication of the photonic local density of states by evanescent modes within the cavity. In particular, we find that radiative heat flow can be enhanced by several orders of magnitude in cavities ranging from nanometer to micrometer scales, depending on the absorber frequency and dipole orientation. These findings suggest that near-field effects may be relevant to polariton chemistry experiments and other systems operating within this cavity length-scale regime. Our results add to the idea that cavities can modify material properties not only by engineering vacuum fluctuations in the strong light-matter coupling regime, but also by controlling radiative dissipation and heat transfer.

title: A low-cost compact muon detector for millikelvin operation
abstract: Ionizing radiation produces correlated errors in superconducting qubits, posing some challenges to quantum error correction. In addition, it causes background events in other superconducting cryogenic devices, such as kinetic inductance detectors and superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors. Cosmic muons are a component of this background that can only be partly shielded against at ground level, but can be tagged by an independent detector inside the cryostat, so that the affected data can be vetoed, or the muon tags incorporated into error correction. We present a low-cost, compact muon detector consisting of two plastic scintillator modules, each read out by a silicon photomultiplier (SiPM), operated in coincidence. We characterize the SiPMs from room temperature down to 10 mK, including the breakdown and upper-limit voltages that define the operating bias range. Operated as a muon counter, the detector measures a coincidence rate that, as expected, is independent of temperature within uncertainties and agrees with analytical and Monte Carlo predictions. Below approximately 8 K, each muon event produces two pulses, one narrow and one broad, an effect that, to our knowledge, has not been reported before. Coincidences with an independent muon detector outside the cryostat confirm that muons are still counted reliably in this regime. By studying the appearance of double pulses as a function of temperature and magnetic field up to 4.5 T, we find a behavior consistent with the phase diagram of a type-II superconductor. This links the double pulses to a superconducting material in the SiPM, likely an adhesion layer or diffusion barrier introduced during manufacturing. The mechanism by which the superconducting state produces the second pulse is not yet understood.

title: From Single-Particle Thermal Asymmetry to Collective Control: Janus Plasmonic Colloids for Photothermal Applications
abstract: Janus nanoheaters provide a route to break the spatial symmetry of thermoplasmonic heating and generate directionally biased thermal gradients at the nanoscale. However, in realistic photothermal scenarios, nanoheaters rarely act as isolated objects, but rather operate within colloidal assemblies where collective thermal and electromagnetic effects reshape the local temperature landscape. Here, we investigate how the intrinsic thermal asymmetry of a single Janus plasmonic nanoheater is transformed when moving from isolated particles to planar random arrays under continuous-wave illumination. Using coupled electromagnetic and steady-state heat-transfer simulations, we first quantify the finite spatial range over which the single-particle Janus signature remains detectable. We show that neighboring nanoheaters introduce two competing effects: a nearly symmetric collective thermal background that screens and homogenizes the Janus factor, and short-range neighbor-induced asymmetries that partially compensate this screening when interparticle distances become comparable to the spatial extent of the single-particle thermal anisotropy. We derive a closed-form analytical model for the array-averaged Janus factor as a function of nanoparticle number and surface density. The model predicts the screening-dominated regime from single-particle quantities and identifies deviations associated with near-field neighbor-induced contributions at higher densities. These results demonstrate a central trade-off for biomedical photothermal applications in continuous-wave operation: collective heating is required to reach relevant temperature increments, but it progressively erases the directional Janus character by thermal homogenization. Our framework provides a practical route to predict and rationally design the spatial temperature distribution in plasmonic assemblies of Janus particles.

summaries.en: Coupled electromagnetic and heat-transfer simulations show that in planar random arrays of Janus plasmonic nanoheaters, collective heating provides the temperature increase needed for photothermal applications while progressively screening the single-particle thermal asymmetry, with short-range neighbor effects partially compensating this screening at high densities as captured by a closed-form model for the array-averaged Janus factor.

title: Photoacoustic-guided reflection-mode wavefront shaping through dynamic biological tissue
abstract: Strong optical scattering limits the depth at which light can be focused and used for imaging in biological tissue. Photoacoustic (PA)-guided wavefront shaping enables non-invasive light focusing in scattering media, but most existing implementations require optical and acoustic access from opposite sides of the sample and a rigidly aligned free-space optical path, which have confined these demonstrations to thin or static samples. Here, we combine a real-valued intensity transmission matrix (RVITM) algorithm with a photoacoustic guidestar (PA-RVITM) in a reflection-mode configuration. Modulated light is delivered through a flexible multimode fiber passing through the central aperture of a focused ultrasound transducer, enabling optical illumination and acoustic detection from the same side of the sample without a free-space combiner. Fiber integration preserved the wavefront shaping performance, and the reflection-mode PA-RVITM system achieved sub-second wavefront optimization with a ~14-fold PA signal enhancement through a diffuser. In ex vivo chicken breast tissue, the enhancement decreased with tissue thickness, reaching ~3.5 through a 2-mm chicken breast layer, with a speckle decorrelation time of ~450 ms. By performing an independent RVITM optimization at each scan position, our system enabled photoacoustic microscopy of a black nylon wire through the same layer, reducing the imaged line width from ~141 {\mu}m to ~102 {\mu}m, close to the nominal diameter of ~100 {\mu}m. This work advances PA-guided wavefront shaping toward a compact, same-side implementation for future biomedical therapeutic and imaging applications.

title: Cavity-tunable Pseudospin-Hall Topology and Edge Transport
abstract: Topological edge states are a hallmark of topological phases, with their existence tied to bulk band topology through bulk-edge correspondence. In photonic pseudospin-Hall systems, these states exhibit pseudospin-momentum locking, with lattice interactions and interface geometry determining each pseudospin's propagation direction. Reversing the pseudospin-dependent propagation direction without altering the lattice configuration or excitation handedness remains a fundamental challenge in controlling topological edge transport. Here, we theoretically and experimentally demonstrate cavity-tunable topological edge transport in a microwave metasurface embedded within a metallic cavity. Varying the cavity height reshapes resonator interactions, driving band inversion and topological phase transition while preserving the lattice geometry. For a fixed domain-wall configuration, this transition reverses the propagation direction associated with each pseudospin while preserving pseudospin-momentum locking. Excitations with the same handedness are observed to launch edge waves propagating in opposite directions at their respective edge-band frequencies determined by the cavity height. These results establish cavity electrodynamics as an external means of controlling the bulk topology and reconfiguring the directional response of topological interfaces, creating new opportunities for topological wave routing in fixed photonic lattice structures.

summaries.en: Cavity height tuning in a microwave metasurface enables reversible pseudospin-dependent topological edge transport via band inversion without altering the lattice geometry.

title: A Reconstruction of Michelson Interference from On--Off Detection Statistics
abstract: This paper reconstructs the Michelson interference phenomenon based solely on the binary (on-off) statistics of a single-photon counter and macroscopic path-difference data, without the a priori assumptions of complex wave superposition or prior spectral information. In contrast to the conventional approach that assumes light as a continuous complex wave function and considers interference between them, this study focuses on the algebraic properties inherent in discrete detection statistics. We verify that the discrete response data collected across various path differences form a positive semi-definite matrix, and apply Herglotz's theorem to this result. Consequently, we show that the harmonic form of the interference fringe is not a consequence of adopting a wave model as an axiom, but rather it is uniquely decomposed into a cosine average of wavenumbers dictated by testable algebraic constraints satisfied by the statistical data. Through this approach, the logical basis of the interference phenomenon can be described by the characteristics of the binary data itself, perfectly aligning with the modern optical experimental environment that relies entirely on discrete event statistics.

summaries.en: Using only binary on-off single-photon detection statistics and macroscopic path-difference data, this paper shows via positive semi-definiteness and Herglotz's theorem that the cosine interference fringe follows uniquely from algebraic constraints on the discrete data, without assuming complex wave superposition.

summaries.ja: 本論文は、単一光子計数器の二元（オン・オフ）統計と巨視的な光路差データのみに基づき、半正定値性の検証とHerglotzの定理を用いて、余弦干渉縞が複素波の重ね合わせを仮定せずとも離散データの代数的制約から一意に導かれることを示す。

title: Void-Free Through-Glass Vias for Multilayer Surface-Electrode Ion Traps
abstract: Through-substrate interconnects are a key technology for scaling surface-electrode ion traps (SEITs) toward large electrode counts and complex architectures. Dielectric substrates such as fused silica offer superior RF performance compared to silicon, but the reliable fabrication of void-free through-glass vias (TGVs) remains challenging. In this work, we demonstrate a SEIT fabricated on a fused silica substrate incorporating TGVs. The via-holes are formed using Selective Laser-Induced Etching and subsequently metallized with gold by electroplating. A patent-pending geometry-assisted bottom-up plating approach enables void-free filling using constant-current electroplating without electrolyte additives or pulsed deposition schemes. Electrical characterization across multiple wafers confirms a TGV-level yield above 98.8 %, demonstrating the robustness and reproducibility of the developed TGV technology. The TGVs are combined with multilayer SEIT fabrication, enabling vertical signal routing to all electrodes while maintaining an unaffected trapping surface without wire bonds. To interface the trap with external control electronics, a glass interposer providing signal fan-out to a larger pitch is designed and fabricated. The trap chip and the interposer are integrated using thermocompression bonding, forming a compact chip-to-chip assembly. The presented technology demonstrates the first fully integrated multilayer SEIT on fused silica incorporating void-free TGVs.

title: Quantum-enhanced phase interrogation of a fiber-optic strain sensor
abstract: Fiber-optic sensors enable high-sensitivity measurements of various physical parameters. Here, we demonstrate a quantum-enhanced interrogation of an all-fiber-optic Fabry-Perot resonator, employing entangled two-photon interference to probe directly strain-induced optical phase shifts. The resonator is interrogated by a narrow-linewidth laser that is frequency-locked to its resonance mode, thereby exploiting the cavity's inherent sensitivity to variations in the fiber length. To access the phase fluctuations transferred to the interrogation field due to external perturbations on the sensor, we implement an in-fiber Mach-Zehnder interferometer readout. This configuration allows the sensor to operate both with classical coherent light and with entangled photon pairs generated via spontaneous parametric down-conversion. Harnessing two-photon entangled states corresponding to an N = 2 NOON state, we experimentally demonstrate a reduction of the measurement noise below the standard quantum limit. These results provide clear evidence of the quantum advantage in enhancing fiber-optic sensors under practical constraints on optical power.

summaries.en: Quantum-enhanced interrogation of an all-fiber Fabry-Perot strain sensor using entangled two-photon NOON-state interference demonstrates measurement noise below the standard quantum limit.
summaries.zh: 利用纠缠双光子NOON态干涉对全光纤法布里-珀罗应变传感器进行量子增强询问，实验证明测量噪声可降至标准量子极限以下。

title: Single and coupled quantum van der Pol oscillators: Wigner-function dynamics, exact qutrit solutions, and synchronization
abstract: We study quantum van der Pol oscillator in which single-photon pumping competes with a nonlinear two-photon dissipative channel to produce a quantum limit cycle, and the question of how two such oscillators with non-identical intrinsic frequencies synchronize in the sense of phase locking when coupled dissipatively to one another. For a single oscillator, starting from a Lindblad description of the dynamics, we derive the exact Wigner-function evolution equation, and show that its Fokker--Planck approximation admits in the appropriate regime an equivalent classical Itô stochastic description that reproduces remarkably well the full Lindblad dynamics. Notably, the stochastic approach provides an efficient means of capturing system dynamics in the semiclassical regime, where a large number of energy eigenstates contribute and direct numerical simulations become computationally demanding. Restricting to the three lowest Fock states and using a parity symmetry, we obtain in closed form the stationary-state density matrix and its Wigner-function representation that displays pronounced nonclassical features. For two non-identical oscillators, we study the full Lindblad dynamics numerically and characterize synchronization through the stationary-state order parameter as a function of frequency mismatch and dissipative coupling. We find that increasing the effective nonlinear dissipative strength suppresses the synchronized region. Restricting the two oscillators to the three-level qutrit subspace, a parity symmetry reduces the stationary-state problem to an exact $41$-dimensional linear system, allowing to compute the synchronization order parameter. In this reduced description, results in the limit of large dissipation agree closely with those from the full dynamics, while exhibiting in the limit of small dissipation a double-peak synchronization structure accompanied by a phase reversal.

summaries.en: This paper derives an exact Wigner-function evolution and an equivalent stochastic description for a single quantum van der Pol oscillator, and analyzes synchronization between two non-identical oscillators via full Lindblad dynamics and an exact 41-dimensional qutrit-subspace solution, finding that stronger effective nonlinear dissipation shrinks the synchronized region.
summaries.zh: 本文推导了单量子范德波尔振子的精确维格纳函数演化及等价的随机描述，并通过完整林德布拉德动力学和精确的41维三能级子空间解分析两个非全同振子的同步，发现有效非线性耗散增强会缩小同步区域。

title: Deterministic and Programmable Fusion for Scalable Generation of Photonic Graph States
abstract: Entanglement in multiphoton graph states is an important resource with various applications, such as measurement-based quantum computing and memory-less quantum repeaters. While some primitive instances have been successfully prepared, scalable generation of large-scale graph states with programmable connections remains an outstanding challenge. Fusion provides a promising "divide-and-conquer" approach by linking smaller resource states into larger, more complex graphs. However, its practical scalability has been limited by the probabilistic nature of conventional fusion protocols, which necessitates extensive hardware overhead and feed-forward resources to achieve deterministic outcomes. Here, we introduce and experimentally demonstrate a deterministic fusion operation with built-in error mitigation, capable of connecting small time-bin-encoded cluster states--originally generated on-demand from a quantum emitter--into larger, reconfigurable photonic graph states of increased sizes. The fusion operation is realized by nondestructively projecting pairs of flying microwave photonic qubits into Bell states using superconducting circuits with in-situ programmability. Crucially, the protocol features active reset and reuse of matter qubits during graph state generation, thereby circumventing the coherence constraints of the quantum emitter and enabling the generation of genuine multipartite entanglement across 13 photonic qubits. Our results establish a scalable framework for photonic graph-state synthesis, paving the way for fault-tolerant measurement-based quantum computation and distributed quantum networks.

summaries.en: This work demonstrates a deterministic, error-mitigated fusion operation using superconducting circuits that connects time-bin-encoded cluster states from a quantum emitter into reconfigurable photonic graph states with genuine multipartite entanglement across 13 photonic qubits.
summaries.zh: 该工作利用超导电路实现了具有内置纠错功能的确定性融合操作，将量子发射器按需产生的时间-bin编码簇态连接成可重构的光子图态，并在13个光子量子比特间实现了真正的多体纠缠。

title: Photon Demultiplexing Using Spatial Routing
abstract: Spatial sectioning of the far-field noncollinear field from spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) is a promising approach for multiparty quantum communication. Although demonstrations with six pairs of users have been reported, the fundamental limits remain unknown. These include the maximum number of channels, the required degree of channel optimization, and the dependence on input parameters. In this paper, we provide a practical framework that answers these questions by connecting input parameters and invoking a design theorem. For a representative configuration, we realize 12 user-pair channels with routing consistency exceeding $0.9999$ at a $12\%$ reduction in photon flux. We further show that sectioning improves the accidental-coincidence budget linearly with the number of channels $N$, allowing the aggregate key rate to scale with the user count. These results provide a design strategy for spatial-division multiplexing of entangled photons analogous to the channel-spacing standards used in wavelength-division networks.

summaries.en: This paper provides a practical design framework and fundamental limits for spatial-division demultiplexing of entangled photons from spontaneous parametric down-conversion, demonstrating 12 user-pair channels with routing consistency above 0.

title: Hyperentanglement in intermediate phase-space planes: benchmarking a photon-pair source for quantum key distribution
abstract: We characterize a source of photon pairs simultaneously entangled in polarization and in the transverse spatial degree of freedom, with the spatial measurements performed in intermediate planes of the fractional Fourier transform. The source consists of two crossed type-I crystals in a non-collinear geometry, such that the transverse variables carry information about the crystal of origin. Detection in the crystal plane reveals this information completely and destroys the polarization entanglement, so that a scheme using the near and far fields as conjugate spatial bases cannot support a parallel polarization channel. In intermediate planes both spatial bases combine position and momentum, such that the which-crystal information is partially erased, and the polarization entanglement survives in all four combinations of spatial bases. Applying Bell and Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen criteria to the same photon pairs certifies both degrees of freedom simultaneously. We evaluate quantum bit error rates and asymptotic secret key rates in each degree of freedom, and find that the source delivers two simultaneously usable channels per photon pair.

summaries.en: A photon-pair source hyperentangled in polarization and transverse spatial modes enables two simultaneous quantum key distribution channels when spatial measurements are performed in intermediate fractional Fourier transform planes that partially erase which-crystal information.

title: Advances in quantum optomechanical control based on cavity cold-atom systems
abstract: Cavity optomechanics represents a frontier research direction in quantum science and technology, centered on the control and exploration of interactions between electromagnetic fields and mechanical motion. Rooted in quantum mechanics, this field realizes efficient coupling and precise manipulation of optical fields and mechanical vibrations through the structural design and precise regulation of optical microcavities and mechanical oscillators, thereby revealing and harnessing novel quantum phenomena. In recent years, cavity optomechanics has evolved into an interdisciplinary frontier integrating quantum optics, condensed matter physics, and quantum precision measurement, exhibiting profound application in both fundamental physics research and quantum information science. With advancements in technologies such as nanomanufacturing and laser cooling, optomechanical interactions have been successfully demonstrated in various experimental systems. Among these platforms, cavity cold-atom systems stand out as one of the ideal platforms for implementing quantum optomechanics. Featuring exceptional environmental isolation, long quantum coherence times, and strong light-matter interaction, these systems provide a crucial testbed for exploring strong and even ultrastrong optomechanical coupling effects as well as rich nonlinear quantum phenomena. This paper reviews the recent progress in optomechanical control and manipulation based on cavity cold-atom systems. We first outline the fundamental principles of standard cavity optomechanical systems. Then, we describe the experimental realization of linear and nonlinear optomechanical couplings in cold-atom systems. After that, we focus on the representative applications of this platform in high-precision quantum sensing, quantum memory, and the preparation of macroscopic nonclassical states. Finally, we give an outlook and challenges in this field.

summaries.en: This review summarizes recent advances in quantum optomechanical control using cavity cold-atom systems, covering linear and nonlinear optomechanical couplings and their applications in high-precision quantum sensing, quantum memory, and macroscopic nonclassical state preparation.
summaries.zh: 本综述总结了基于腔冷原子系统的量子光力控制研究进展，涵盖线性与非线性光力耦合及其在高精度量子传感、量子存储和宏观非经典态制备中的应用。
summaries.ja: 本レビューは、空洞冷原子系を用いた量子光学力学制御の最近の進展をまとめ、線形・非線形光学力学結合と、高精度量子センシング、量子メモリ、巨視的非古典状態の生成への応用を概説する。

title: Loss-Tolerant Measurement-Device-Independent QKD over Untrusted Repeaters via High-Dimensional Time-Bin Multiplexing
abstract: We propose a loss-tolerant measurement-device-independent quantum key distribution (MDI-QKD) protocol using time-bin-multiplexed single photons entangled with local qubits stored in nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers. In each round, Alice and Bob each send a single multiplexed photon to an untrusted intermediary, Charlie. Each photon first becomes entangled with Charlie's NV-center qubits; Charlie then performs entanglement swapping between his NV qubits to establish EPR pairs between Alice's and Bob's local qubits. With $d$ time bins per photon, $\log_2 d + 1$ EPR pairs can be generated per transmitted photon, substantially increasing the probability of EPR-pair creation under limited channel bandwidth. To further mitigate the effects of prolonged memory storage, the protocol employs a memory-insensitive (MI) architecture, where multiple banks of qubits and multiplexed photon routing reduce the effective memory lifetime requirements. This approach enhances loss tolerance, enabling higher secret key rates and secure key distribution over longer distances compared to conventional single-photon protocols. Using the Lo-Chau EPR-QKD framework and Shor-Preskill reduction, we prove that the protocol is secure without trusting intermediate nodes, making it suitable for quantum networks with untrusted repeaters.

summaries.en: The authors propose a loss-tolerant measurement-device-independent QKD protocol that uses time-bin multiplexed single photons entangled with nitrogen-vacancy center qubits at an untrusted intermediary to generate multiple EPR pairs per photon and prove its security via the Lo-Chau framework and Shor-Preskill reduction.
summaries.zh: 作者提出了一种容忍损耗的测量设备无关量子密钥分发协议，利用与氮空位中心量子比特纠缠的时间-bin复用单光子在不可信中间节点生成多个EPR对，并通过Lo-Chau框架和Shor-Preskill归约证明了其安全性。
summaries.ja: 著者らは、窒素空孔中心量子ビットと絡み合った時間ビン多重化単一光子を信頼できない中間ノードで用いて光子あたり複数のEPR対を生成する、損失耐性のある測定器非依存量子鍵配送プロトコルを提案し、Lo-Chau枠組みとShor-Preskill還元によりその安全性を証明した。

title: Actuation-Aware Pinching-Antenna Placement Under Blockage and User Mobility
abstract: Existing placement studies for pinching-antenna systems (PASS) usually assume that antenna movement is instantaneous and free. In practice, actuators move at finite speeds and must pause radiation while repositioning. This makes performance depend on consecutive antenna positions, turning placement into an edge-weighted longest-path problem on a temporal trellis. We also show that an obstacle blocks a wider range of antenna positions as it approaches the user, causing sudden performance drops that make multi-step lookahead essential, and that once obstacle height is included every blockage event shadows at least a fixed minimum length of waveguide. We give an exact offline solution with complexity O(TMS) and bound the per-slot loss of a W-step receding-horizon policy by O(1/W). Measurements show that the required lookahead window is set by shadow width rather than by waveguide length. Across 20 random seeds, the exact policy delivers 17.7% higher max-min throughput than per-slot optimization under blockage, and matches it when no blockers are present.

summaries.en: This paper formulates actuation-aware pinching-antenna placement under blockage and user mobility as an edge-weighted longest-path problem on a temporal trellis, provides an exact offline solution with complexity O(TMS), and bounds the per-slot loss of a W-step receding-horizon policy by O(1/W), achieving 17.
summaries.zh: 本文将阻塞和用户移动下考虑致动器有限速度的夹持天线放置建模为时间网格上的边加权最长路径问题，给出了复杂度为O(TMS)的精确离线解，并将W步滚动时域策略的每时隙损失界定为O(1/W)，在阻塞场景下比逐时隙优化获得高17.
summaries.ja: 本論文は、遮断とユーザ移動下でのアクチュエーションを考慮したピンチングアンテナ配置を時間トレリス上の辺重み付き最長路問題として定式化し、計算量O(TMS)の厳密なオフライン解を与えるとともに、Wステップの後退ホライズン方策のスロット当たり損失をO(1/W)で抑え、遮断時にはスロットごとの最適化より17.

title: Continued fractions and passive ladder networks for acoustic impedances: the baffled piston and the horn
abstract: Lumped-element networks give transparent, passive models of acoustic impedances whose low- and high-frequency limits can be read from the circuit, but a systematic, arbitrarily accurate construction for non-rational impedances is lacking. Continued fractions, one- and two-point Padé approximants and their identity with ladder networks and Cauer synthesis are introduced in tutorial form and applied to two examples: the radiation impedance of a baffled circular piston and the throat impedance of a horn with a piston mouth. The even contraction of the piston's continued fraction has positive coefficients, certified by interval arithmetic for the first 100 pairs, and yields a ladder of positive resistances, masses and compliances; with 14 elements the error is 4e-4 up to ka = 5. Beranek's four-element network is, to about 2%, the order-two two-point Padé approximant. A horn modelled as a cascade of waveguide sections is a continued fraction whose tail is the mouth impedance; the infinite exponential horn is a periodic continued fraction, an exact high-pass ladder. The piston networks are passive at every certified order (up to 202 elements) and are extended without changing existing elements; for a finite horn the error of the mouth network passes one to one to the throat impedance.
subjects: Audio and Speech Processing (eess.AS) ; Classical Physics (physics.class-ph)

summaries.en: Continued fractions, Padé approximants, and Cauer ladder synthesis are presented in tutorial form and applied to construct arbitrarily accurate passive lumped-element networks for the radiation impedance of a baffled circular piston and the throat impedance of a horn.
summaries.zh: 本文以教程形式介绍了连分式、帕德逼近和Cauer梯形网络综合，并将其应用于为带障板圆形活塞的辐射阻抗和号筒喉部阻抗构造任意精度的无源集总元件网络。
summaries.ja: 連分数、パデ近似、カウアー梯子網合成をチュートリアル形式で導入し、無限バッフル付き円形ピストンの放射インピーダンスとホーンのスロートインピーダンスに対する任意精度の受動集中定数網の構成に適用した。

title: To Stack or Not to Stack? Jacobian Conditioning and the Benefits of Depth in Metasurface-Based Linear Transformation Synthesis
abstract: This paper investigates when and why stacking programmable metasurfaces into Stacked Intelligent Metasurfaces (SIMs) improves linear transformation synthesis at a fixed phase-control budget. The analysis shows that algebraic Jacobian rank alone is insufficient to characterize practical synthesis, which also depends on the strength and balance of the sensitivity directions generated by the available controls. A layer-resolved analysis of the cascade model explains how inter-layer propagation can generate complementary sensitivity directions. The relevance of this mechanism is then assessed using an S-parameter multiport model that includes electromagnetic coupling and multiple scattering. Numerical results in near- and far-field sensing scenarios show that distributing the same control resources across multiple layers can strengthen weak transformation directions, improve Jacobian conditioning, and substantially enhance synthesis accuracy. These findings explain why increasing depth can offer benefits that are not obtained by simply enlarging a single programmable surface, and identify layer complementarity and Jacobian conditioning as useful criteria for SIM architecture design.

summaries.en: Stacking programmable metasurfaces into stacked intelligent metasurfaces can improve linear transformation synthesis at a fixed phase-control budget by generating complementary sensitivity directions that enhance Jacobian conditioning and synthesis accuracy, effects not achievable by simply enlarging a single programmable surface.
summaries.zh: 在固定的相位控制预算下，将可编程超表面堆叠成堆叠智能超表面能够通过产生互补的敏感方向来改善线性变换合成，从而增强雅可比条件数和合成精度，而单纯扩大单个可编程表面无法获得这些效果。
summaries.ja: 固定された位相制御予算の下で、プログラマブルメタサーフェスを積層してスタック型インテリジェントメタサーフェスとすることで、相補的な感度方向が生成され、ヤコビアンの条件付けと合成精度が向上し、単一のプログラマブル表面を拡大するだけでは得られない利点がもたらされる。
